title: Association between levels of persistent organic pollutants in adipose tissue and cryptorchidism in early childhood: a case-control study.
ehr_evidence: Adipose tissue biopsies were taken during surgery, and chemical concentrations were measured by gas chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry. Obstetric data were obtained from medical records, and breastfeeding data were collected via questionnaires.
summary: Case-control study assessing the association between prenatal exposure to persistent organic pollutants (PCBs, PCDD/Fs, PBDEs) measured in adipose tissue and congenital cryptorchidism in early childhood.
key_findings: Total-TEq was positively associated with cryptorchidism after adjustment [OR 3.21 (95% CI 1.29–9.09), p=0.02].
Sum of PCDD/Fs was positively associated with cryptorchidism after adjustment [OR 3.69 (95% CI 1.45–10.9), p=0.01].
Sum of PCBs was close to significant [OR 1.92 (95% CI 0.98–4.01), p=0.07].
Sum of PBDEs was not associated with cryptorchidism [OR 0.86 (95% CI 0.47–1.54), p=0.61].
Unadjusted chemical concentrations showed no significant associations with cryptorchidism risk.
captured_features: Adipose tissue concentrations of PCBs, PCDD/Fs, PBDEs, and total-TEq
population: boys operated for cryptorchidism (cases) or inguinal/umbilical hernia or hydrocele (controls) in Finland and Denmark, aged 0-5 years (Finland) or no limit (Denmark)
limitations: control group included boys with inguinal hernia which is associated with cryptorchidism
recruitment at surgical departments limits generalizability to mild cases
potential inclusion of acquired undescended testes in cases
inability to adjust for lipid content of adipose samples
recall bias for Danish mothers' data collected ~10 years later
lack of data on children's body size
